title: UP BOARD CLASS 9 — Chemistry | Chemical Reactions Types
description: Subject-wise test on Chemical Reactions Types (Chemistry) for UP BOARD CLASS 9. 10Q.
subject: upbo9-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding the characteristics of particles of matter?

options.text: Particles of matter are continuously moving.
Particles of matter have spaces between them.
Particles of matter attract each other.
Particles of matter are visible to the naked eye.

questions.explanation: Particles of matter are extremely small and cannot be seen with the naked eye. The other options (continuous movement, spaces between them, and attraction) are all fundamental characteristics of matter particles.
questions.subject: upbo9-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly describes a liquid?

options.text: It has a definite shape and a definite volume.
It has a definite volume but no definite shape.
It has neither a definite shape nor a definite volume.
Its particles are very tightly packed with strong intermolecular forces.

questions.explanation: Liquids take the shape of the container they are in, meaning they do not have a definite shape, but their volume remains constant. Solids have definite shape and volume, while gases have neither.
questions.subject: upbo9-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding the characteristics of particles of matter?

options.text: Particles of matter have spaces between them.
Particles of matter are continuously moving.
Particles of matter attract each other.
Particles of matter are visible to the naked eye.

questions.explanation: Particles of matter are extremely small and cannot be seen with the naked eye. Options A, B, and C are correct characteristics of matter particles.
questions.subject: upbo9-chemistry

questions.question: What is the smallest particle of an element that can exist independently and retain all its chemical properties?
questions.explanation: An atom is defined as the smallest particle of an element that can exist independently (though some reactive atoms don't, the definition refers to its fundamental nature) and retains all its chemical properties. A molecule is formed by two or more atoms. An ion is a charged atom or molecule. A compound is formed by two or more different elements chemically combined.
questions.subject: upbo9-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following states of matter has a definite volume but no definite shape?
questions.explanation: Liquids have a definite volume but take the shape of the container they are in, hence they do not have a definite shape. Solids have both definite volume and shape, while gases have neither.
questions.subject: upbo9-chemistry

questions.question: What is the smallest particle of an element that can exist independently and retain all its chemical properties?
questions.explanation: An atom is defined as the smallest particle of an element that can take part in a chemical reaction and retains all the properties of that element. Molecules are formed by two or more atoms. Ions are charged atoms or molecules. Compounds are formed by two or more different elements chemically combined.
questions.subject: upbo9-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true about the particles in a gas?

options.text: They are tightly packed and vibrate about their fixed positions.
They are loosely packed and can slide over one another.
They are far apart, move randomly and rapidly.
They have definite shape and volume.

questions.explanation: Gases have the weakest intermolecular forces. Their particles are very far apart, move randomly and rapidly in all directions, occupying the entire volume of the container. Options A, B, and D describe solids, liquids, and solids respectively.
questions.subject: upbo9-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a homogeneous mixture?
questions.explanation: A homogeneous mixture has a uniform composition throughout. Salt solution (salt dissolved in water) is an example where the salt particles are uniformly distributed and are indistinguishable from the water. Sand and water, oil and water, and iron filings and sulfur are all heterogeneous mixtures where components are visibly separate.
questions.subject: upbo9-chemistry

questions.question: In a chemical reaction, 4.9 g of magnesium (Mg) reacts completely with 3.2 g of oxygen (O) to form magnesium oxide (MgO). What is the mass of magnesium oxide formed?
questions.explanation:
According to the Law of Conservation of Mass, mass can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction. Therefore, the total mass of the reactants must be equal to the total mass of the products.
Mass of reactants = Mass of Magnesium + Mass of Oxygen
Mass of reactants = 4.9 g + 3.2 g = 8.1 g
Mass of product (Magnesium oxide) = 8.1 g
questions.subject: upbo9-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a pure substance?
questions.explanation: Water is a chemical compound made of hydrogen and oxygen in a fixed ratio, hence it is a pure substance. Air, milk, and soil are heterogeneous or homogeneous mixtures.
questions.subject: upbo9-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true for gases?

options.text: They have a definite shape and a definite volume.
They have a definite volume but no definite shape.
They have neither a definite shape nor a definite volume.

questions.explanation: Gases completely fill the container they are kept in, taking its shape and volume. Their particles are far apart and move randomly, leading to no definite shape or volume.
questions.subject: upbo9-chemistry

questions.question: Which state of matter has a definite volume but no definite shape?
questions.explanation: Liquids take the shape of the container they are in, thus having no definite shape, but they maintain a constant volume. Solids have both definite shape and volume, while gases have neither.
questions.subject: upbo9-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a homogeneous mixture?
questions.explanation: A homogeneous mixture has a uniform composition throughout. Sugar solution, once dissolved, forms a uniform mixture where sugar particles are evenly distributed in water, and its components cannot be seen separately. Sand and water, oil and water, and polluted air are heterogeneous mixtures.
questions.subject: upbo9-chemistry

questions.question: An atom consists of protons, neutrons, and electrons. Which of these particles carries a negative charge?
questions.explanation: Electrons are subatomic particles that orbit the nucleus and carry a negative charge. Protons carry a positive charge, and neutrons are electrically neutral. The nucleus contains protons and neutrons.
questions.subject: upbo9-chemistry

questions.question: According to the Law of Conservation of Mass, what happens to the total mass of reactants and products in a chemical reaction?
questions.explanation: The Law of Conservation of Mass states that mass can neither be created nor destroyed in an ordinary chemical reaction. Therefore, the total mass of the reactants must be equal to the total mass of the products.
questions.subject: upbo9-chemistry

questions.question: Why do gases diffuse faster than liquids and solids?

options.text: Gas particles are held together by strong forces.
Gas particles have large intermolecular spaces and high kinetic energy.
Gas particles have a definite shape.

questions.explanation: Gases have the weakest intermolecular forces of attraction and the highest kinetic energy among the three states of matter. This allows their particles to move very rapidly and randomly, leading to faster diffusion compared to liquids and solids where particles are more closely packed and have less freedom of movement.
questions.subject: upbo9-chemistry

questions.question: If 12g of carbon reacts completely with 32g of oxygen to form 44g of carbon dioxide, what mass of carbon dioxide will be formed if 6g of carbon reacts with 16g of oxygen?
questions.explanation: This question applies the Law of Constant Proportions (or Law of Definite Proportions). In carbon dioxide (CO₂), carbon and oxygen combine in a fixed mass ratio. From the first reaction: Carbon : Oxygen = 12g : 32g = 3 : 8. If 6g of carbon reacts with 16g of oxygen, the ratio is again 6g : 16g = 3 : 8. Since the reactants are in the same fixed ratio and react completely, they will form carbon dioxide according to the Law of Conservation of Mass: Mass of CO₂ = Mass of Carbon +
questions.subject: upbo9-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding the properties of gases?

options.text: Gases have indefinite shape and indefinite volume.
Particles in gases are widely spaced and move randomly.
Gases have strong intermolecular forces of attraction.

questions.explanation: Gases have very weak intermolecular forces of attraction, which allows their particles to move freely and randomly, resulting in indefinite shape and volume and high compressibility.
questions.subject: upbo9-chemistry

questions.question: A substance that cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical reactions is called:
questions.explanation: An element is the simplest form of matter that cannot be further divided into simpler substances by ordinary chemical methods.
questions.subject: upbo9-chemistry

questions.question: Which subatomic particle carries a negative charge and revolves around the nucleus of an atom?
questions.explanation: Electrons are negatively charged subatomic particles that occupy the space outside the nucleus and revolve in specific orbits. Protons are positively charged, and neutrons are neutral, both residing in the nucleus.
questions.subject: upbo9-chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following processes represents a chemical change?
questions.explanation: Burning of a candle involves the combustion of wax, producing new substances like carbon dioxide and water vapor, which is a chemical change. Melting, dissolving, and boiling are physical changes as no new substances are formed.
questions.subject: upbo9-chemistry

questions.question: Calculate the molar mass of water (H₂O). (Given: Atomic mass of H = 1 u, O = 16 u)
questions.explanation: Molar mass of H₂O = (2 × Atomic mass of H) + (1 × Atomic mass of O) = (2 × 1 u) + (1 × 16 u) = 2 u + 16 u = 18 u. Therefore, the molar mass is 18 g/mol.
questions.subject: upbo9-chemistry

questions.question: According to Dalton's Atomic Theory, atoms of the same element are:

options.text: Different in mass and chemical properties
Identical in mass and chemical properties
Identical in mass but different in chemical properties
Different in mass but identical in chemical properties

questions.explanation: One of the fundamental postulates of Dalton's Atomic Theory states that all atoms of a given element are identical in mass and chemical properties. (Note: This postulate was later modified with the discovery of isotopes, but for Class 9 understanding of Dalton's theory, this is the correct interpretation).
questions.subject: upbo9-chemistry

questions.question: How many moles are present in 9 grams of water (H₂O)? (Given: Molar mass of H₂O = 18 g/mol)
questions.explanation: Number of moles = Given mass / Molar mass = 9 g / 18 g/mol = 0.5 mol
questions.subject: upbo9-chemistry

questions.question: Assertion (A): Isotopes are atoms of the same element having the same atomic number but different mass numbers. Reason (R): Isotopes have a different number of protons but the same number of neutrons.

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is true: Isotopes are atoms of the same element (meaning same atomic number/protons) but differ in mass number. This difference in mass number arises because they have a different number of neutrons. Reason (R) is false: Isotopes have the *same* number of protons (as they are the same element) but a *different* number of neutrons.
